question: What is the primary function of the nurses' station on a hospital ward?

options.A: It is used strictly for storing heavy surgical instruments.
options.B: It serves as the central command and communication hub for the ward.
options.C: It acts as a private waiting room exclusively for visitors.
options.D: It functions as the main kitchen facility for patient meals.

explanation: The nurses' station coordinates patient care, documentation, and communication across the entire ward. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is it important for student midwives to know the ward layout early?

options.A: To quickly locate emergency equipment during critical situations
options.B: To help out with hospital maintenance
options.C: To avoid doing desk work
options.D: To know where to hide during doctor rounds

explanation: Knowing where supplies and exits are located saves precious seconds when managing urgent cases like postpartum bleeding. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which hospital ward is specifically dedicated to monitoring high-risk pregnancies before delivery?

options.A: Pediatric ward
options.B: Antenatal ward
options.C: Postnatal ward
options.D: Gynecological ward

explanation: The antenatal ward provides specialized care and observation for women experiencing complications during pregnancy before they go into labor. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h2)

question: A newly delivered mother and her healthy baby need routine postpartum monitoring and breastfeeding support. Where should she be admitted?

options.A: Intensive care unit
options.B: Labor ward
options.C: Postnatal ward
options.D: Antenatal ward

explanation: The postnatal ward is specifically designed to care for mothers and newborns following a successful delivery. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which department is primarily responsible for dispensing life-saving obstetric drugs like oxytocin?

options.A: The pharmacy department
options.B: The physiotherapy department
options.C: The medical records department
options.D: The hospital laundry unit

explanation: Pharmacies store, manage, and dispense all medications prescribed for patients in the hospital. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is a close working relationship between the labor ward and the blood bank essential?

options.A: To ensure laboratory staff can assist with normal vaginal deliveries
options.B: To provide extra beds for mothers waiting to be discharged home
options.C: To quickly secure blood products during severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: To reduce the cost of routine urinalysis testing for pregnant women

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is a major cause of maternal mortality, making fast access to cross-matched blood critical. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h3)

question: At what point in the hospital stay should discharge planning ideally begin?

options.A: During the final post-delivery ward round
options.B: After the patient has already left the ward
options.C: On the day of admission
options.D: Only when the doctor signs the discharge ticket

explanation: Early discharge planning anticipates the patient's needs and ensures a seamless transition back home. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of the triage process when a patient first arrives at the facility?

options.A: To collect full payment for hospital services before any care is given
options.B: To complete all research questionnaires required by the hospital
options.C: To prioritize care based on the severity of the patient's condition
options.D: To assign the patient to a permanent room in the private ward

explanation: Triage ensures that emergency cases receive immediate medical attention while stable patients wait their turn. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h4)

question: What does contemporaneous documentation mean in midwifery practice?

options.A: Copying past medical records into a new computer system
options.B: Writing up all patient notes at the end of the work week
options.C: Recording care and events as they happen in real time
options.D: Allowing patients to write their own clinical observations

explanation: Contemporaneous notes prevent omissions and errors that occur when health workers rely on memory later. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice when transferring a patient to another department?

options.A: Ensuring vital signs are stable before moving the individual
options.B: Providing a clear referral letter stating the reason for transfer
options.C: Sending the patient without any written notes or verbal handover
options.D: Accompanied by a trained staff member if the condition is critical

explanation: Sending a patient without proper communication or documentation compromises their safety and continuity of care. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h5)

question: Who forms the multidisciplinary team that works together on a hospital ward?

options.A: Only senior consultant obstetricians and gynecologists
options.B: Various healthcare professionals collaborating for patient care
options.C: Hospital administrative managers and billing officers exclusively
options.D: External visitors and family members of admitted patients

explanation: A multidisciplinary team includes midwives, doctors, pharmacists, and support staff working together toward patient recovery. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h6)

question: A student midwife overhears a colleague discussing a patient's private medical condition in the hospital cafeteria. What ethical principle is being violated?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Confidentiality
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Discussing patient details in public spaces breaches professional confidentiality and patient trust. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T1#BMP119_U1_T1_h6)

question: What primary feeling do patients often experience when they enter a hospital or clinic setting?

options.A: Excitement and curiosity
options.B: Vulnerability and fear
options.C: Indifference and quiet
options.D: Boredom and impatience

explanation: Patients in clinical settings are often dealing with health uncertainties, which naturally makes them feel vulnerable and afraid. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is understanding safety rules important during your very first days on the hospital ward?

options.A: It helps you avoid senior staff members who might report minor mistakes.
options.B: It ensures you can complete all charting tasks without help from doctors.
options.C: It protects the fragile trust patients place in individuals wearing the uniform.
options.D: It allows you to finish your clinical rotation much earlier than scheduled.

explanation: Patients trust healthcare workers immediately based on their role and uniform, making safe practices essential from day one to preserve that trust. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of good professional conduct for a midwife?

options.A: Arriving early to ensure a smooth handover
options.B: Guarding patient privacy on social media
options.C: Gossiping about patients at the nurses' station
options.D: Using respectful language with colleagues

explanation: Gossiping about patients violates confidentiality and demonstrates poor professional conduct. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h2)

question: A patient is bleeding heavily after birth, and the ward is extremely busy. What is the best way to handle your demeanor?

options.A: Express your frustration openly so everyone knows how serious it is
options.B: Raise your voice to command everyone to move faster
options.C: Leave the room until the senior doctor arrives to take charge
options.D: Maintain a calm demeanor to reassure the patient and staff

explanation: Remaining calm during emergencies keeps the team focused and prevents the patient from panicking further. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must midwives keep their fingernails short and free of artificial extensions in the clinical area?

options.A: Long and artificial nails trap bacteria and can scratch patients.
options.B: Artificial nails are too expensive for student budgets.
options.C: Hospital management simply prefers a traditional look.
options.D: Long nails make writing in patient case notes difficult.

explanation: Nails harbor microorganisms that can easily be transmitted during patient examinations, and long edges risk injuring delicate skin. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for avoiding strong perfumes and heavy makeup on the maternity ward?

options.A: It distracts male doctors from performing their clinical duties.
options.B: Strong scents can trigger nausea in pregnant and postpartum women.
options.C: Cosmetics react poorly with the harsh soaps used in the hospital laundry.
options.D: Patients will assume the midwife is not taking her job seriously.

explanation: Pregnant and postpartum women often experience heightened sensitivities to smells, making mild or unscented hygiene products essential. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which ethical principle means acting in the best interest of the patient to promote their well-being?

options.A: Justice
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Accountability
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Beneficence refers to taking positive steps to help and benefit the patient under your care. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h4)

question: A patient demands more of your time than other women in the postnatal ward who have greater medical needs. Which ethical principle helps you handle this fairly?

options.A: Non-maleficence
options.B: Paternalism
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Justice

explanation: Justice requires that nursing care is distributed fairly and equitably based on medical need, not social or financial standing. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which body is legally responsible for regulating nursing and midwifery education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: The Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: The Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: The West African Health Organization

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body empowered by law to regulate the profession and discipline erring practitioners in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h5)

question: What does professional accountability mean for a student midwife on the labor ward?

options.A: You can blame your clinical supervisor if a medication mistake happens.
options.B: You are answerable for your own actions, errors, and clinical omissions.
options.C: You only take orders from doctors and hold no personal responsibility.
options.D: You are protected from legal consequences because you are still learning.

explanation: Every healthcare practitioner, including students under supervision, must take personal responsibility for the care they provide. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h5)

question: What defines an ethical dilemma in a clinical setting?

options.A: A disagreement between two doctors over a surgical technique
options.B: A scenario where competing moral principles make a clear choice difficult
options.C: A patient refusing to pay hospital bills after delivery
options.D: A situation where equipment is broken and care must be delayed

explanation: An ethical dilemma happens when valid moral values or duties clash, leaving no simple right or wrong answer. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h6)

question: A pregnant woman refuses a medically necessary blood transfusion due to her religious beliefs. What is the most appropriate initial step for the midwife?

options.A: Discharge her immediately from the hospital for non-compliance
options.B: Explore her concerns calmly and involve senior colleagues or ethics support
options.C: Report her directly to the police for endangering her unborn child
options.D: Administer the blood transfusion secretly while she is asleep

explanation: Open communication and consultation help navigate complex refusals while respecting patient autonomy and seeking safe alternatives. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T2#BMP119_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which regulatory body sets the professional code of conduct for midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) is the official body that sets and maintains standards for nursing and midwifery education and practice across the country. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why must Nigerian midwives combine clinical skills with a strong understanding of healthcare ethics?

options.A: To ensure the hospital receives more funding from the government
options.B: To protect patient dignity while maintaining professional and legal safety
options.C: To prevent patients from asking too many questions about their treatment
options.D: To speed up the discharge process for postnatal mothers

explanation: Ethics ensures that patients are treated with respect and helps protect the midwife from professional misconduct issues. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h1)

question: What does a patient's right to information require a midwife to do before starting a procedure?

options.A: Show the patient her medical file in the records room
options.B: Consult the village head before touching the patient
options.C: Explain the diagnosis and treatment options in clear language
options.D: Have the hospital administrator sign a financial clearance form

explanation: Patients must understand what is happening to their bodies so they can make informed choices about their care. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in labour states she does not want a routine episiotomy. What action aligns best with her patient rights?

options.A: Discharge her immediately from the labour ward for non-compliance
options.B: Perform the episiotomy anyway because staff know what is best for delivery
options.C: Ask her husband to override her decision and give consent instead
options.D: Respect her refusal and explore alternative ways to protect her perineum

explanation: Competent patients have the legal right to decline specific interventions, which means midwives need to adapt care plans accordingly. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following actions represents a clear breach of patient confidentiality?

options.A: Sharing clinical findings with the attending doctor on duty
options.B: Discussing a patient's HIV test results openly in the hospital staff canteen
options.C: Locking the antenatal clinic registers in a secure cabinet before closing
options.D: Asking a student midwife to read a file under direct supervision

explanation: Talking about private patient information in public spaces allows unauthorized people to overhear, which violates confidentiality. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is strict confidentiality especially crucial in maternal and child health care?

options.A: It ensures that doctors do not interfere with nursing duties
options.B: It makes record-keeping easier for the health records department
options.C: It builds trust and encourages women to seek care for stigmatized conditions
options.D: It prevents the government from auditing hospital finances

explanation: When women know their personal information is safe, they are more honest about their health history and more willing to attend clinics. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h3)

question: What three key elements must be present for informed consent to be valid?

options.A: Witness testimony, marriage certificate, and age verification
options.B: Hospital stamp, doctor signature, and cash payment
options.C: Voluntariness, capacity, and adequate information
options.D: Emergency status, doctor approval, and family consent

explanation: Valid consent requires a capable patient making a voluntary choice after receiving complete details about the care. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h4)

question: A husband insists on signing the consent form for his wife's caesarean section while she is fully alert and capable of deciding. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Accept the husband's signature because he is the head of the household
options.B: Acknowledge the husband's support but obtain direct consent from the wife
options.C: Cancel the surgery immediately until the entire family agrees
options.D: Ask the doctor to perform the surgery using emergency override rules

explanation: A competent adult woman holds the sole legal right to consent to or refuse medical procedures on her own body. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h4)

question: When can a midwife legally provide emergency treatment without obtaining prior informed consent?

options.A: When the patient is sleeping peacefully in the postnatal ward
options.B: Whenever a senior doctor gives a verbal instruction over the phone
options.C: Whenever the patient disagrees with the prescribed treatment plan
options.D: When the patient is unconscious and faces an immediate threat to life

explanation: Emergency exceptions permit immediate life-saving care when a patient cannot speak for themselves and delaying would cause death or severe harm. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why does the law allow the emergency doctrine during critical obstetric situations?

options.A: It speeds up the paperwork required for health insurance claims
options.B: It gives midwives total authority over all hospital departments
options.C: It assumes any reasonable person would want life-saving intervention
options.D: It protects the hospital from paying compensation to the family

explanation: This rule bridges the gap when consent is impossible, prioritizing survival over paperwork until the crisis passes. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h5)

question: What defines an ethical dilemma in clinical midwifery practice?

options.A: An equipment shortage in the main operating theatre
options.B: A situation where two or more moral principles or duties compete with each other
options.C: A disagreement between a nurse and a doctor over shift rosters
options.D: A delay in receiving salary payments from the health board

explanation: Ethical dilemmas happen when right actions conflict, forcing the midwife to carefully weigh competing values. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary role of a midwife acting as a patient advocate?

options.A: Protecting the patient's rights and safety within the healthcare system
options.B: Convincing patients to accept any treatment doctors prescribe
options.C: Reporting fellow midwives to the disciplinary committee
options.D: Ensuring hospital rules are obeyed before patient comfort

explanation: Advocacy centers on standing up for the client's welfare, voice, and rights, especially when they are vulnerable. [learn more](BMP119_U1_T3#BMP119_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which germs picked up from touching patients or surfaces are the main cause of hospital infections?

options.A: Resident flora
options.B: Transient flora
options.C: Normal spores
options.D: Deep dermal fungi

explanation: Transient microorganisms are picked up from surfaces or patients and are easily spread if hand hygiene is missed. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is washing your hands so important in clinical settings?

options.A: It eliminates all resident flora completely
options.B: It breaks the chain of infection by removing surface microbes
options.C: It replaces the need for wearing clean gloves
options.D: It permanently sterilizes the deep layers of the skin

explanation: Washing or sanitizing hands targets transient pathogens, stopping them from moving between patients and equipment. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h1)

question: When should a midwife clean their hands before doing a sterile procedure?

options.A: Immediately before the procedure
options.B: After cleaning the patient's skin
options.C: Only after removing sterile gloves
options.D: Only if visible dirt is present

explanation: Hand hygiene before a clean task prevents introducing outside germs into sterile body sites. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why must you clean your hands after touching objects near a patient, like a bed rail or call button?

options.A: Surroundings easily pick up and harbor patient germs
options.B: Hospital equipment is treated with harsh chemical preservatives
options.C: It satisfies hospital accreditation paperwork
options.D: It prevents skin dryness caused by touching metal surfaces

explanation: High-touch surfaces near the bed are often contaminated with patient flora and can spread infection just as direct touch does. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h2)

question: How long should a standard handwash with soap and water take?

options.A: 2 to 3 minutes
options.B: 10 to 15 seconds
options.C: 5 to 10 seconds
options.D: 40 to 60 seconds

explanation: Spending nearly a minute scrubbing ensures all surfaces of the hands are properly exposed to friction and soap. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why use a paper towel to turn off the water tap after washing your hands?

options.A: To keep the bathroom floor dry and safe from slips
options.B: To absorb excess moisture left behind on your wrists
options.C: To polish the metal tap handle for infection control inspections
options.D: To prevent touching a contaminated surface with clean hands

explanation: Turning off the tap with your bare hands would transfer germs from the handle right back onto your freshly washed skin. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the recommended alcohol percentage for an effective hand sanitizer?
explanation: Concentrations below 60% fail to kill microorganisms effectively, while extremely high concentrations evaporate too quickly. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h4)

question: A midwife puts alcohol gel on her hands and wipes them dry with a cloth towel because they feel wet. What does this do?

options.A: It protects her skin from chemical irritation
options.B: It helps the alcohol evaporate much faster
options.C: It sterilizes the cloth towel for future use
options.D: It reduces the effectiveness of the hand antisepsis

explanation: Alcohol rub needs time to air dry completely on the skin to achieve its full germ-killing effect; wiping it away early ruins the process. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h4)

question: When do you strictly need soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Whenever you enter a private antenatal room
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material
options.C: When visiting patients who are stable and recovering
options.D: Before taking a patient's routine temperature

explanation: Visible dirt, blood, or body fluids must be physically washed away with soap and water because sanitizers cannot penetrate heavy soil. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why must you use soap and water rather than alcohol when caring for a patient with a Clostridioides difficile infection?

options.A: Alcohol cannot kill bacterial spores
options.B: Water neutralizes the toxins produced by the bacteria
options.C: Alcohol destroys the spores and makes them spread faster
options.D: Soap has a pleasant fragrance that covers foul odors

explanation: C. difficile produces resilient spores that resist alcohol rubs, requiring physical friction and rinsing with soap and water to remove them. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT allowed because it traps germs and gets in the way of hand hygiene?

options.A: Plain smooth wedding bands
options.B: Short, clean natural nails
options.C: Artificial fingernails
options.D: Short-sleeved nursing uniforms

explanation: Artificial nails harbor heavy bacterial and fungal growth that resists standard hand hygiene, making them a major infection hazard. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is regular hand cream important for midwives who wash their hands frequently?

options.A: It speeds up the evaporation time of liquid soap
options.B: It prevents dry skin cracking that can harbor germs
options.C: It replaces the need for using alcohol-based rubs
options.D: It leaves a scented film that repels hospital insects

explanation: Healthy, uncracked skin acts as a natural barrier against infection, whereas dry, broken skin traps harmful bacteria. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T1#BMP119_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of obtaining a baseline vital sign measurement?

options.A: To calculate the correct dosage of routine vitamins
options.B: To determine the exact gestational age of the fetus
options.C: To diagnose specific infectious diseases immediately
options.D: To provide a reference point for comparing future readings

explanation: A baseline gives the midwife a normal starting measurement for that specific patient so that any dangerous changes later on can be spotted quickly. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why should a midwife allow a newly arrived patient to rest briefly before taking vital signs?

options.A: Physical exertion and anxiety can temporarily alter the readings
options.B: Hospital regulations require a mandatory waiting period for records
options.C: It gives the midwife time to prepare the patient file
options.D: Patients cannot speak clearly immediately upon entering the clinic

explanation: Walking to the clinic or feeling nervous can falsely raise heart rate and blood pressure, so a short rest ensures accurate results. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which temperature route is generally considered the safest and most commonly used for routine adult screening?

options.A: Rectal
options.B: Axillary
options.C: Sublingual
options.D: Gastric

explanation: The armpit method avoids mucous membranes, making it safe, non-invasive, and very practical for general clinic use. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why should an oral temperature not be measured immediately after a patient drinks a hot cup of tea?

options.A: Hot fluids cause immediate contraction of the salivary glands
options.B: The hot liquid will falsely elevate the thermometer reading
options.C: It will permanently damage the glass bulb of the thermometer
options.D: The patient will be unable to hold the thermometer under the tongue

explanation: Ingesting hot or cold substances alters the local temperature in the oral cavity, leading to inaccurate results. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h2)

question: What does the term 'rhythm' refer to when assessing a patient's pulse?

options.A: The overall strength and volume of the blood flow
options.B: The total number of beats counted in one full minute
options.C: The specific anatomical site where the pulse is felt
options.D: The regularity or spacing between individual beats

explanation: Pulse rhythm describes whether the heart beats in a steady, even pattern or skips beats irregularly. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h3)

question: A midwife feels a weak, barely perceptible pulse on a woman experiencing severe postpartum hemorrhage. How is this pulse quality best described?

options.A: Bounding
options.B: Arrhythmic
options.C: Thready
options.D: Tachycardic

explanation: A weak, thin, and difficult-to-feel pulse is classically described as thready, often seen when blood volume is severely reduced. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why do midwives often count respirations while pretending to continue taking the pulse?

options.A: Hospital protocol strictly forbids looking directly at the patient's chest
options.B: Patients tend to consciously alter their breathing if they know it is being watched
options.C: Patients will accidentally hold their breath if spoken to during this time
options.D: It is mathematically required to calculate the respiratory-pulse ratio simultaneously

explanation: People naturally change their breathing speed and depth when they focus on it, so covert observation yields more accurate baseline data. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following describes tachypnea in an adult patient?

options.A: Deep, labored breathing associated with diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: An abnormally rapid breathing rate above 20 breaths per minute
options.C: An abnormally slow breathing rate below 10 breaths per minute
options.D: A complete and sudden cessation of breathing movements

explanation: The prefix tachy- means fast, so tachypnea refers specifically to a respiratory rate higher than the normal adult range. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h4)

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if the cuff used is much too small for the patient's arm?

options.A: It has no effect on the final measurement
options.B: It makes it impossible to hear any sounds
options.C: It produces a falsely low reading
options.D: It produces a falsely high reading

explanation: A narrow cuff requires extra pressure to compress the large arm tissue, which artificially inflates the blood pressure numbers. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h5)

question: Where should the midwife place the stethoscope bell when auscultating blood pressure on the arm?

options.A: Across the midpoint of the biceps muscle belly
options.B: On the inner wrist over the radial pulse point
options.C: Directly over the bony prominence of the elbow joint
options.D: Over the brachial artery in the antecubital fossa

explanation: The antecubital fossa houses the brachial artery, making it the correct anatomical site for hearing Korotkoff sounds clearly. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h5)

question: When is the best time for a midwife to record measured vital signs in the patient's case notes?

options.A: At the end of the entire shift before going home
options.B: During the next morning handover meeting
options.C: Only when the patient's condition begins to worsen
options.D: Immediately after completing the assessment

explanation: Recording values right away prevents memory lapses and ensures other healthcare workers have access to current data. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which combination of vital sign changes is a classic warning sign of developing hemorrhagic shock in a postnatal woman?

options.A: Falling blood pressure and a rising pulse rate
options.B: Falling temperature and an elevated respiratory rate
options.C: Rising blood pressure and a slowing pulse rate
options.D: Normal blood pressure and a normal respiratory rate

explanation: As blood volume drops, the heart beats faster to compensate, while blood pressure eventually drops as shock progresses. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T2#BMP119_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why must wrinkles be avoided on a patient's bed?

options.A: They make the room look untidy to visitors
options.B: They prevent friction and skin breakdown
options.C: They interfere with the ward laundry schedule
options.D: They cause the mattress to wear out faster

explanation: Smooth linen protects delicate skin layers from continuous pressure and friction, which are major causes of painful pressure sores. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is shaking used bedsheets strictly prohibited during bed making?

options.A: It spreads dust and micro-organisms into the air
options.B: It creates too much noise for sleeping patients
options.C: It tangles the linen making folding difficult later
options.D: It stretches the fabric and ruins the elastic edges

explanation: Shaking textiles releases dust mites, skin flakes, and infectious pathogens into the surrounding ward air where they can be inhaled. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the correct way to stack clean linen on a bedside chair before making a bed?

options.A: In the exact reverse order of their use
options.B: In a random pile for quick grabbing
options.C: Sorted strictly by color and fabric type
options.D: With the bottom sheets placed right on top

explanation: Stacking items in reverse order of use means the first item you need is right on top, reducing unnecessary handling and saving time. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h2)

question: A student midwife finishes stripping an unoccupied bed and notices a stain on the plastic mattress cover. What action should be taken next?

options.A: Proceed with making the bed since clean sheets will cover it
options.B: Clean and disinfect the mattress cover before placing new linen
options.C: Cover the stain quickly with an extra draw sheet
options.D: Turn the mattress upside down to hide the stain

explanation: Mattress covers must be properly sanitized between patients to prevent cross-infection, regardless of whether clean linen will be placed over them. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is the patient asked to roll over a central hump of rolled linen during an occupied bed change?

options.A: It keeps the patient warm while the top covers are removed
options.B: It allows the midwife to change the sheets without moving the patient out of bed
options.C: It prevents the patient from falling off the narrow hospital bed
options.D: It provides extra back support while the patient rests

explanation: Rolling over the linen hump lets the midwife pull clean sheets across the empty half of the mattress while the patient rests safely on the other half. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h3)

question: During an occupied bed make, what is the best immediate action when the patient expresses sudden dizziness?

options.A: Ignore it briefly until the bottom sheet is fully tucked
options.B: Ask a relative to hold her steady while you tuck the sheet
options.C: Stop the procedure immediately and check her vital signs
options.D: Work twice as fast to finish the bed so she can lie flat

explanation: Patient safety always overrides task completion; dizziness can indicate a drop in blood pressure requiring immediate attention. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main reason why top covers on a post-operative bed are fan-folded to the side or foot?

options.A: To prevent dust from settling on the clean pillowcase
options.B: To save time when the laundry personnel come to collect linen
options.C: To allow sunlight to warm up the mattress surface directly
options.D: To make transferring the patient from a trolley quick and easy

explanation: Fan-folding eliminates barriers, allowing theatre staff to slide the patient straight from the stretcher onto the bed without lifting through tangled blankets. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which item is most critical to position near a post-operative recovery bed before the patient's arrival?

options.A: Fresh flowers in a glass vase
options.B: Suction and oxygen equipment
options.C: A heavy woolen winter blanket
options.D: Extra reading books and magazines

explanation: Post-operative patients are vulnerable to airway obstruction and respiratory depression, making immediate access to suction and oxygen vital. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the correct action when handling soiled linen removed from a patient's bed?

options.A: Drop it on the floor until all the beds in the ward are finished
options.B: Fold it neatly and place it on a nearby bedside chair temporarily
options.C: Place it directly into a designated hamper without letting it touch your uniform
options.D: Shake it vigorously to check for misplaced patient valuables

explanation: Keeping soiled linen away from your body and depositing it immediately prevents the transfer of pathogens to your clothes and ward surfaces. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is it dangerous to place used hospital linen on the floor?

options.A: It violates general room ventilation standards
options.B: It causes the fabric to stain permanently from dust
options.C: It spreads micro-organisms across the floor and increases contamination
options.D: It makes the floor slippery for other walking patients

explanation: Floors harbor heavy microbial loads; putting linen on the floor transfers germs to the fabric and kicks dust particles into the air. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h5)

question: What correct body posture should a midwife use when making a fixed-height low bed?

options.A: Bend at the knees and hips while keeping the back straight
options.B: Twist your torso sideways to reach across the sheets faster
options.C: Lean your chest heavily against the mattress edge for balance
options.D: Keep the knees locked straight and bend completely from the waist

explanation: Bending the knees shifts workload to powerful leg muscles and protects the lumbar spine from strain and injury. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the final safety action a midwife must take immediately after finishing an occupied bed?

options.A: Spray strong air freshener around the unit
options.B: Ensure side rails are raised and the bed is locked
options.C: Turn off the ward overhead lighting
options.D: Leave the bedside curtains fully drawn

explanation: Raising side rails and locking wheels prevents accidental patient falls and uncoordinated movement after the bed has been adjusted. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T3#BMP119_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary reason midwives assist postpartum mothers with personal hygiene?

options.A: To measure daily fluid intake and urine output precisely
options.B: To speed up the involution of the uterine muscle
options.C: To promote physical comfort and prevent infections
options.D: To complete hospital administrative discharge forms

explanation: Helping mothers stay clean makes them feel comfortable and stops harmful germs from causing infections during recovery. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why must a midwife observe a mother carefully while she cleans herself after childbirth?

options.A: To ensure she uses only hospital-approved herbal soaps
options.B: To teach her relatives how to perform perineal care at home
options.C: To check for signs of dizziness, fatigue, or sudden distress
options.D: To evaluate how quickly her surgical wound is closing up

explanation: Postpartum women can easily become weak or dizzy from blood loss, so watching them closely prevents bathroom falls. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which direction should a midwife follow when washing a patient's body to control infection?

options.A: From the lower limbs upward toward the chest and face
options.B: From the cleanest areas toward the dirtiest areas
options.C: From the left side of the body directly to the right side
options.D: From the most sensitive skin areas outward to the limbs

explanation: Washing from clean to dirty stops germs from being spread onto areas that are clean and vulnerable to infection. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of changing wash water and basins frequently during a bed bath?

options.A: To allow the patient time to rest between the washing steps
options.B: In order to test the patient's skin for sudden temperature changes
options.C: So that hospital soap does not run out during the procedure
options.D: To keep the water warm and prevent spreading microorganisms

explanation: Dirty water gets cold quickly and carries bacteria, so fresh warm water keeps the patient comfortable and safe. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h2)

question: How should a midwife test the water temperature before beginning a bed bath?

options.A: By using a clinical thermometer to get an exact reading
options.B: By asking the patient to plunge a finger into the water
options.C: By splashing a few drops of water onto the patient's toes
options.D: By dipping the inner wrist into the basin of water

explanation: The inner wrist has sensitive skin that easily detects if water is too hot, protecting the patient from accidental burns. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h3)

question: A postpartum patient is receiving a bed bath. Which body part should be washed first?

options.A: Chest and abdomen
options.B: Lower legs and feet
options.C: Face and eyes
options.D: Perineal area

explanation: Washing starts at the cleanest part, which is the face and eyes, and moves downward toward dirtier areas. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a major risk when performing oral care on an unconscious patient?

options.A: Cracking the dental enamel with force
options.B: Causing a sudden spike in blood pressure
options.C: Aspiration of fluids into the lungs
options.D: Swallowing the soft sponge applicator

explanation: Unconscious patients cannot swallow properly, so excess liquid can easily flow into their windpipe and lungs. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why should an unconscious patient's head be turned to the side during mouth care?

options.A: In order to make the teeth easier to see in low lighting
options.B: To allow excess liquids and secretions to drain out safely
options.C: So that the tongue falls backward and blocks the windpipe
options.D: To stop the patient from biting down on the cleaning tools

explanation: Turning the head sideways lets gravity pull liquids out of the mouth instead of letting them pool in the throat. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the correct technique when brushing tangled hair for a bedridden patient?

options.A: Working in small sections from the hair ends up to the scalp
options.B: Soaking the entire scalp in harsh antiseptic liquid first
options.C: Cutting out the tangled knots immediately with blunt scissors
options.D: Pulling the comb firmly from the scalp straight down to the tips

explanation: Starting at the ends and moving upward prevents painful pulling and reduces hair breakage. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary purpose of performing hair care for a hospitalized woman?

options.A: Curing severe postpartum hemorrhage conditions
options.B: Checking the scalp for signs of lice or skin irritation
options.C: Keeping the hair free from painful mats and tangles
options.D: Improving her personal comfort and mental well-being

explanation: Hair care improves comfort and hygiene, but it has no direct medical effect on heavy uterine bleeding. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is keeping a postpartum mother's fingernails short particularly important?

options.A: So that intravenous lines can be inserted into her hands easily
options.B: To prevent her from accidentally scratching her newborn baby
options.C: In order to speed up the healing of cracked skin on her fingers
options.D: To stop her from picking at her postpartum abdominal stitches

explanation: Long fingernails can easily scratch a baby's delicate skin when the mother holds or feeds the infant. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which patient group requires special medical caution before a midwife trims their toenails?

options.A: Patients recovering from mild postpartum emotional blues
options.B: Patients with diabetes or poor peripheral circulation
options.C: Young mothers who are exclusively breastfeeding their babies
options.D: Women who had normal, uncomplicated vaginal deliveries

explanation: Diabetes and poor blood flow cause slow healing and high infection risks, making accidental cuts during nail trimming very dangerous. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h6)

question: How can a midwife best protect a patient's dignity during a bed bath?

options.A: By uncovering only the specific body part currently being washed
options.B: By finishing the entire bathing procedure as quickly as possible
options.C: By asking family members to leave the room permanently
options.D: By performing the bath without talking to lower the awkwardness

explanation: Keeping unwashed areas covered with blankets protects the patient's modesty and maintains body warmth. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why should midwives encourage patients to help with their own hygiene care?

options.A: To promote personal independence and self-reliance
options.B: So that nurses have time to complete paperwork tasks
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the bath
options.D: In order to reduce hospital spending on laundry detergent

explanation: Allowing patients to do what they can helps them regain confidence and encourages faster physical recovery. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T4#BMP119_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of keeping your feet wide apart when preparing to lift a patient?

options.A: To create a wide and stable base of support
options.B: To reduce the weight of the patient significantly
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling backward
options.D: To increase the speed of the lifting movement

explanation: A wider stance widens your base of support, which improves overall balance and stability when exerting force. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why should a nurse or midwife avoid twisting the spine while holding a heavy load?

options.A: Twisting places dangerous rotational stress on the lower back discs
options.B: It cuts off blood circulation to the arms and hands
options.C: Twisting causes the leg muscles to lock up immediately
options.D: It makes the load feel twice as heavy as it actually is

explanation: Combining spinal rotation with a heavy load puts immense shearing force on the spinal discs, leading to injury. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which position is most appropriate for a postpartum woman who is experiencing shortness of breath?

options.A: Sims position
options.B: Lithotomy position
options.C: Fowler's position
options.D: Supine position

explanation: Elevating the head of the bed into Fowler's position allows the diaphragm to descend easier, improving lung expansion and easing breathing. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h2)

question: A student midwife needs to perform a routine rectal examination on a patient. Which position should she prepare the patient in?

options.A: Fowler's position
options.B: Lateral position
options.C: Supine position
options.D: Sims position

explanation: The Sims semi-prone position exposes the anal area clearly and relaxes the gluteal muscles for rectal procedures. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h2)

question: How often should an immobile bedridden patient be turned and repositioned?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Only when they complain of pain
options.C: Every four hours
options.D: Once every shift

explanation: Turning a patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on capillaries, preventing tissue ischemia and pressure ulcers. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is a draw sheet used when moving a patient up in bed instead of pulling them directly by their arms?

options.A: It distributes the lifting force evenly and prevents skin shearing
options.B: It eliminates the need for a second nurse to help
options.C: It stops the patient from rolling onto their stomach
options.D: It makes the patient feel lighter to lift off the mattress

explanation: A draw sheet minimizes friction and shearing forces that damage fragile skin and underlying tissues during sliding movements. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for allowing a patient to 'dangle' on the edge of the bed before standing up?

options.A: To allow the patient's leg muscles to completely relax
options.B: To give the nurse time to clean the wheelchair seat
options.C: To check if the patient's nightwear is properly fastened
options.D: To prevent dizziness caused by orthostatic hypotension

explanation: Dangling allows blood pressure to stabilize after moving from lying to sitting, preventing sudden fainting or dizziness. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which action is critical when setting up a wheelchair for a patient transfer?

options.A: Removing both footrests permanently from the chair
options.B: Lowering the wheelchair seat to its absolute lowest setting
options.C: Placing the wheelchair directly parallel to the bed
options.D: Locking the wheels of both the bed and the wheelchair

explanation: Locking all wheels prevents the bed or chair from slipping away during the transfer, which is a major cause of falls. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which complication of immobility is best prevented by encouraging deep breathing exercises and frequent position changes?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Muscle atrophy
options.C: Hypostatic pneumonia
options.D: Orthostatic hypotension

explanation: Deep breathing and position changes help expand lung bases and clear pooled secretions, preventing lung infections. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h5)

question: A pregnant patient on strict bed rest for antepartum hemorrhage is at high risk for blood clots in her lower legs. Which condition is she developing a risk for?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Pressure ulceration
options.C: Pulmonary edema
options.D: Muscle contracture

explanation: Sluggish blood flow in immobile legs, combined with the hypercoagulable state of pregnancy, greatly increases deep vein thrombosis risk. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h5)

question: What key detail must be recorded in the nursing notes after assisting a patient with a transfer?

options.A: The name of the nursing supervisor on duty that day
options.B: The time, transfer method used, and patient's tolerance
options.C: The exact brand name of the wheelchair used
options.D: The patient's personal opinion on the hospital food

explanation: Accurate documentation must capture the exact intervention performed and how the patient responded to ensure continuity of care. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the very first action a midwife should take if a patient suddenly feels extremely dizzy while being assisted to walk?

options.A: Leave the patient standing briefly to find a stethoscope
options.B: Ask the patient to walk faster to finish the exercise quickly
options.C: Document the dizziness in the chart while the patient stands
options.D: Safely guide or lower the patient back to a resting position

explanation: Patient safety comes first; stopping the activity and preventing a fall takes immediate priority over all other actions. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T5#BMP119_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary use of a handheld urinal in the ward?

options.A: Collecting stool samples from bedridden clients
options.B: Washing the perineal area after delivery
options.C: Collecting urine from male patients
options.D: Measuring fluid intake during a shift

explanation: Urinals are shaped to fit male anatomy so patients can urinate easily while lying or sitting in bed. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why should you respond quickly when a bedridden patient asks for a bedpan?

options.A: To prevent the bedpan from cooling down too much
options.B: To comply with hospital administrative rules
options.C: To finish your shift duties much faster
options.D: To prevent the patient from falling while trying to walk alone

explanation: Prompt assistance stops patients from getting up unassisted, which often leads to dangerous falls and injuries. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which type of bedpan works best for a patient with a fractured hip?

options.A: A pediatric training potty
options.B: A standard deep metal bedpan
options.C: A fracture bedpan with a low profile
options.D: An oversized bariatric bedpan

explanation: Fracture pans have a shallow, tapered end that slips easily under patients who cannot lift their hips high. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the main reason for placing a waterproof pad under a patient's hips?

options.A: To protect the bed linens from accidental spills or leaks
options.B: To provide extra warmth during cold weather
options.C: To elevate the pelvis higher than the chest
options.D: To make the mattress softer for the patient

explanation: The waterproof barrier stops urine or stool from soaking into the mattress and sheets, saving time on linen changes. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h2)

question: How do you position a weak patient who cannot lift their hips onto a bedpan?

options.A: Roll the patient to one side, place the pan against the buttocks, and roll them back
options.B: Pull strongly on the drawsheet to drag the patient upward
options.C: Ask two visitors to lift the patient's torso into the air
options.D: Keep the head of the bed fully raised at a ninety-degree angle

explanation: Rolling minimizes strain on both the patient's body and your spine compared to lifting the pelvis manually. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h3)

question: What bed position is best when sliding a standard bedpan underneath a patient?

options.A: Flat
options.B: Trendelenburg
options.C: Semi-Fowler's
options.D: High Fowler's

explanation: A flat bed lets the patient bridge their hips upward with minimal effort and prevents spills during placement. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why is the head of the bed usually elevated while a patient uses a bedpan?

options.A: It stops the patient from falling asleep too quickly
options.B: Gravity helps natural elimination when sitting upright
options.C: It keeps the bedsheets completely dry
options.D: It makes it easier to change intravenous fluids

explanation: An upright posture uses gravity to make bowel movements and urination easier, mimicking normal bathroom posture. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h4)

question: What item must always be left within a patient's reach before you walk away?

options.A: The hospital telephone
options.B: A glass of ice water
options.C: The call bell
options.D: The medication chart

explanation: The call bell ensures the patient can call for help as soon as they finish eliminating. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h4)

question: Where is the safest temporary place to set a covered bedpan after removing it?

options.A: On the floor right next to the nurse's station
options.B: On a designated chair or utility surface near the bed
options.C: On the patient's overbed food table
options.D: On the clean linen trolley in the hallway

explanation: Keeping bedpans away from eating areas prevents cross-contamination and maintains ward hygiene. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the correct action to take immediately after sliding the bedpan out from beneath a patient?

options.A: Leave the room to wash hands immediately
options.B: Cover the bedpan to reduce odors and exposure
options.C: Wash the patient's face with warm water
options.D: Shake the bedpan vigorously to check for leaks

explanation: Covering the pan right away controls unpleasant odors and limits the spread of germs. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h5)

question: In which direction should a female patient's perineal area be wiped after elimination?

options.A: From back to front
options.B: From front to back
options.C: In circular scrubbing motions
options.D: From side to side

explanation: Wiping from front to back stops bacteria from the anal area from entering the vagina and urethra, lowering infection risks. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why is it important to dry the perineal skin thoroughly after cleansing?

options.A: Dry skin absorbs hospital medications much faster
options.B: It stops the patient from feeling cold
options.C: Moisture trapped against the skin leads to irritation and breakdown
options.D: It prevents the bedsheets from getting wrinkled

explanation: Trapped moisture softens the skin barrier, making it vulnerable to chafing, rashes, and pressure sores. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h6)

question: What tool should you use to accurately measure liquid urine output from a bedpan?

options.A: A standard drinking glass
options.B: A clean surgical basin
options.C: A graduated measuring cylinder
options.D: A disposable plastic medicine cup

explanation: Graduated cylinders have clear volume markings designed to measure liquid output accurately for clinical charts. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which of these findings should be reported immediately to the doctor or senior midwife?

options.A: A moderate amount of soft brown stool
options.B: Clear yellow urine with no foul odor
options.C: Normal urine output over a twenty-four-hour period
options.D: Bright red blood mixed in the stool or urine

explanation: Blood in the urine or stool is an abnormal sign that requires prompt medical review and care. [learn more](BMP119_U2_T6#BMP119_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of clinical documentation in midwifery practice?

options.A: To replace verbal communication entirely
options.B: To fulfill government tax requirements
options.C: To ensure patient safety and continuity of care
options.D: To provide reading material for medical students

explanation: Clear records allow every healthcare provider involved in a mother's care to know what has been done and what needs to happen next, preventing dangerous errors. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is verbal communication alone considered insufficient in a busy maternity unit?

options.A: Doctors refuse to listen to verbal reports from midwives
options.B: Patients prefer reading notes to listening to staff
options.C: Spoken words can be easily forgotten or misunderstood during shift changes
options.D: Hospital regulations strictly forbid talking between shifts

explanation: A busy ward creates many distractions, making written records essential for accurate memory retention and safe handover. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following measurements is a standard vital sign for an adult maternity patient?

options.A: Vision sharpness
options.B: Blood pressure
options.C: Hair growth rate
options.D: Daily weight gain

explanation: Blood pressure, pulse, temperature, and respiration are core vital signs checked routinely during antenatal, labor, and postnatal care. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the most serious consequence of a midwife guessing a patient's vital signs instead of measuring them?

options.A: The temperature chart will look too neat
options.B: Dangerous conditions like postpartum hemorrhage may go unnoticed
options.C: The patient will complain about the cost of care
options.D: The hospital electricity bill will increase

explanation: Accurate measurements catch early signs of shock or infection, allowing prompt treatment that saves lives. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is another common name for the temperature chart used in clinical wards?

options.A: Fluid balance sheet
options.B: Birth register
options.C: TPR chart
options.D: Drug Kardex

explanation: TPR stands for Temperature, Pulse, and Respiration, which are the primary trends tracked graphically on this specific chart. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why is graphing vital signs on a temperature chart better than writing them only as numbers in a paragraph?

options.A: It makes the handwriting look neater than normal prose
options.B: It gives a quick visual picture of how the patient's condition is changing over time
options.C: It prevents patients from reading their own medical records
options.D: It saves paper by squeezing more numbers into a smaller space

explanation: A graph lets a midwife instantly spot upward or downward trends, such as a creeping temperature that signals an infection. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h3)

question: What essential detail must accompany every single entry written in the midwives notes?

options.A: The patient's religion and home address
options.B: The current weather outside the ward
options.C: Date, time, signature, and professional designation
options.D: The name of the hospital director

explanation: Accountability requires knowing exactly when an observation was made and who made it, complete with their professional title. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following phrases is best to write in the midwives notes?

options.A: Patient complained of lower abdominal pain, rated 7 out of 10, at 14:00 hours
options.B: Patient refused to cooperate with staff members because she is stubborn
options.C: Patient is acting strangely and complaining too much about pain today
options.D: Patient looks fine and nothing unusual happened during the morning shift

explanation: Professional documentation relies on objective facts, exact times, and clear descriptions rather than emotional judgments or vague opinions. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the correct way to correct a writing mistake in a clinical record?

options.A: Scribble over the mistake multiple times until it is pitch black
options.B: Draw a single neat line through the error so it can still be read, then write the correction
options.C: Tear out the entire page and start the document again
options.D: Use liquid correction fluid to cover it up completely

explanation: Crossing out an error neatly preserves transparency, proving no data was dishonestly hidden if the record is ever examined legally. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why are clinical records considered legal documents in a court of law?

options.A: They serve as official evidence of the care provided during a malpractice or negligence investigation
options.B: They can be used to settle financial debts between patients and hospitals
options.C: They are written using special government-approved ink
options.D: They are automatically signed by a magistrate before admission

explanation: If a clinical outcome is questioned legally, courts rely heavily on the written medical record to determine what care took place. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h5)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for in the SBAR handover communication tool?

options.A: Supplies
options.B: Situation
options.C: Symptoms
options.D: Staffing

explanation: In the SBAR tool, S stands for Situation, which helps the speaker state clearly what is happening right now. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is a structured handover method important during a shift change?

options.A: It removes the need to write anything in the nurses notes
options.B: It prevents important patient details from being missed during the transfer of responsibility
options.C: It forces midwives to finish their shift much faster
options.D: It prevents patients from listening to private hospital discussions

explanation: Structure ensures consistency so that incoming staff receive all vital safety information without relying on memory. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T1#BMP119_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a shift handover in a midwifery unit?

options.A: To assess the punctuality of incoming nurses
options.B: To replace formal patient case notes entirely
options.C: To transfer patient responsibility and ensure continuous care
options.D: To give staff time to catch up on personal gossip

explanation: Handover guarantees that incoming staff know the current condition and plan for every patient, preventing any break in safety or treatment. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why can a rushed or chaotic handover put a mother and newborn at risk?

options.A: It forces the doctor to discharge patients too early
options.B: Vital clinical details might be missed by the incoming team
options.C: It causes the hospital electricity to shut down suddenly
options.D: It prevents mothers from breastfeeding their babies

explanation: When information is left out due to rushing, staff may not notice early warning signs of complications like postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following describes an objective clinical statement?

options.A: The woman is complaining too much about normal labor pains
options.B: Mother looks like she does not care about her newborn baby
options.C: Patient refused vaginal examination at 10:00 hours after explanation
options.D: Patient is simply being very difficult and uncooperative today

explanation: Objective statements record exact facts and actions without adding personal judgment or emotional bias. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h2)

question: Name the feature that makes a handover report interactive.

options.A: Reading the report out loud as fast as humanly possible
options.B: Allowing the receiving midwife to ask clarifying questions
options.C: Writing the notes in pencil so mistakes can be erased
options.D: Leaving the room before the new shift arrives

explanation: An interactive handover is a two-way dialogue where doubts are cleared up immediately, unlike a one-way monologue. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h2)

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the SBAR communication framework?

options.A: Admission
options.B: Aftercare
options.C: Anticipation
options.D: Assessment

explanation: In SBAR, 'Assessment' refers to sharing your current clinical findings and vital sign measurements for the patient. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h3)

question: A midwife tells the incoming shift about a woman's previous two normal deliveries and her current admission details. Which part of SBAR is this?

options.A: Background
options.B: Situation
options.C: Recommendation
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Past obstetric history and details of how the admission unfolded form the background context of the patient's care. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a priority item to mention during a labor ward handover?

options.A: The brand of soap the patient used to wash her clothes at home
options.B: The latest fetal heart rate auscultation results
options.C: The current cervical dilation and membrane status
options.D: Any outstanding laboratory investigations like packed cell volume

explanation: Personal home details that do not affect clinical outcomes are irrelevant to emergency maternity handovers. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why must fetal heart rate findings be highlighted during every labor handover?

options.A: To calculate the total hospital bill for the newborn baby
options.B: To catch early signs of fetal distress before it becomes catastrophic
options.C: To prove to the hospital management that the midwife was working
options.D: To decide what clothes the mother will wear after delivery

explanation: Fetal well-being changes rapidly during labor, making continuous awareness of heart rate patterns essential for saving infant lives. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is a common environmental barrier to an effective shift handover?

options.A: Loud background noise in a busy clinical area
options.B: Using blue ink instead of black ink in the register
options.C: Having too many chairs in the staff common room
options.D: Writing reports on standard white paper sheets

explanation: Excessive noise makes it hard to hear vital clinical numbers and instructions, leading to misunderstandings. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h5)

question: How can a facility reduce the negative impact of staff hierarchy during handovers?

options.A: By encouraging an open culture where junior staff can freely ask questions
options.B: By banning junior midwives from attending the morning briefing
options.C: By making senior midwives complete all handovers in complete silence
options.D: By punishing junior staff who request clarification on patient charts

explanation: Creating a welcoming environment ensures that junior midwives feel safe speaking up if they spot a missing detail or potential error. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h5)

question: What does the legal nursing maxim state about care that is not documented?

options.A: If it was not documented, legally it was never done
options.B: Unrecorded care is considered twice as effective
options.C: Written records matter less than verbal memory
options.D: Only doctors are allowed to write notes in the register

explanation: In courts of law and professional tribunals, only written evidence in the clinical record proves that care was actually delivered. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h6)

question: A midwife signs off on a shift report stating that all postpartum observations are normal without actually checking the patients. What is the ethical implication of this action?

options.A: It saves time for the incoming shift during a busy morning
options.B: It breaches professional ethics and can lead to disciplinary action
options.C: It is acceptable as long as no patient complains later on
options.D: It is standard practice for experienced senior midwives

explanation: Falsifying records or documenting unperformed checks is professional misconduct that endangers patients and violates regulatory standards. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T2#BMP119_U3_T2_h6)

question: What primary purpose does a client's case note serve in a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Recording the daily market prices of hospital drugs
options.B: Listing the names of visitors allowed on the ward
options.C: Providing a clear, chronological trail of care
options.D: Tracking the monthly salary of hospital staff

explanation: Case notes are designed to record the timeline of clinical events so that any healthcare provider can understand what care was given. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must a midwife record clinical events as close to the time of care as possible?

options.A: To avoid buying extra pens for the ward
options.B: To impress the senior nursing officer on duty
options.C: To finish the shift duties much faster
options.D: To prevent memory lapses and ensure accurate details

explanation: Writing down observations immediately stops important clinical details from being forgotten as the shift gets busier. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following actions should a midwife take first during client admission?

options.A: Force the client to sign her discharge papers early
options.B: Send the relatives out of the hospital gate immediately
options.C: Welcome the client courteously to reduce anxiety
options.D: Demand full payment before taking any vital signs

explanation: A warm welcome helps calm the woman and builds trust between her and the healthcare team right from the start. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h2)

question: A woman arrives at the labor ward in active contraction. What is the most important initial documentation task for the admitting midwife?

options.A: Listing all the food items she brought in her bag
options.B: Recording the exact time of arrival and baseline vital signs
options.C: Drawing a detailed map of her village home address
options.D: Calculating the total hospital utility bills for the month

explanation: Baseline observations and arrival times give an immediate picture of maternal and fetal status upon entry to the ward. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why must a midwife conduct a personal belongings inventory jointly with the client or her relative?

options.A: To select the best clothes for the baby to wear home
options.B: To prevent disputes and accusations of missing items
options.C: To calculate the total financial wealth of the family
options.D: To find out which designer brands the client prefers

explanation: Doing an inventory together ensures both parties agree on what was brought in, protecting everyone from claims of theft. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h3)

question: What should happen after recording a client's personal belongings on the admission inventory form?

options.A: The document should be torn up and thrown away
options.B: The midwife must keep the items in her personal locker
options.C: Both the midwife and the client must sign the list
options.D: Only the hospital gateman needs to sign the paper

explanation: Signatures from both the health worker and the client validate that the inventory list is accurate and complete. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h3)

question: What information is typically found in a discharge summary?

options.A: Diagnosis, treatment given, and condition upon leaving
options.B: A list of all cleaning chemicals used in the ward
options.C: The personal phone numbers of all ward doctors
options.D: The daily menu served in the hospital canteen

explanation: The summary recaps what happened during admission so that community clinics know what treatment was carried out. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following topics is NOT optional when educating a mother before she leaves the hospital?

options.A: Favorite television programs for newborns
options.B: The current political leaders in the country
options.C: Danger signs for both mother and baby
options.D: The history of the hospital building

explanation: Mothers must know warning signs so they can return to the clinic quickly if complications arise at home. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h4)

question: How should a midwife correct an error made inside a client's paper case note?

options.A: Tear out the entire page so nobody sees the mistake
options.B: Apply thick correction fluid until the paper is completely white
options.C: Draw a single neat line through it and write the correction
options.D: Scratch the ink out aggressively with a razor blade

explanation: Drawing a single line keeps the original entry readable while showing where the correction was made, which maintains legal transparency. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is back-dating a clinical entry considered unacceptable professional practice?

options.A: It causes the hospital pen to run out of ink too quickly
options.B: It makes the handwriting look untidy to the medical director
options.C: It uses up too many pages in the official hospital register
options.D: It misrepresents the actual timeline of care given to the client

explanation: Records must reflect the exact time events happened; changing dates distorts clinical facts and compromises legal accountability. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T3#BMP119_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of infection prevention in a maternity ward?

options.A: To speed up the discharge process for postnatal mothers
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of running laboratory tests
options.C: To completely eliminate all bacteria from the hospital air
options.D: To break the chain of transmission between patients and staff

explanation: Infection prevention focuses on stopping microorganisms from spreading among patients and healthcare workers in clinical spaces. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why are pregnant and postpartum women in busy Nigerian wards particularly vulnerable to hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: They refuse to take prophylactic antibiotics prescribed by the attending doctor
options.B: They spend more days admitted to the ward than general medical patients do
options.C: They share personal clothing and bedding with other mothers in the same bay
options.D: Their immune defenses are often lowered by conditions like prolonged labour or surgery

explanation: Procedures like caesarean sections and events like ruptured membranes create entry points for pathogens in an already stressed body. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which group of patients should standard safety precautions be applied to in the ward?

options.A: Every patient admitted to the healthcare facility
options.B: Only women undergoing surgical delivery procedures
options.C: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases
options.D: Patients who display visible symptoms of fever

explanation: Standard precautions are universal and must be used for all patients regardless of their known or suspected infection status. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why must a midwife treat all body fluids as potentially infectious during clinical care?

options.A: Hospital policy requires gloves for routine non-clinical ward rounds
options.B: Detergents are too weak to kill germs in wet clinical environments
options.C: Infection status is often unknown and visual checks are unreliable
options.D: Laboratory results take too long to arrive from the main hospital

explanation: Many infectious carriers show no outward signs of illness, making universal precautions necessary for every interaction. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h2)

question: When is it most appropriate to use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: When moving quickly between stable postnatal mothers
options.B: Before touching a patient who has intact skin
options.C: Immediately after removing clean examination gloves
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Alcohol rubs cannot remove organic material and dirt effectively, so physical washing with soap and water is required when hands are dirty. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h3)

question: A midwife is about to assist with a spontaneous vaginal delivery where heavy blood and fluid splashes are expected. What is the correct sequence of action regarding PPE?

options.A: Put on gown, mask, eye protection, and gloves before the procedure begins
options.B: Wash hands with soap and water after the delivery baby is safely placed
options.C: Wear only heavy-duty utility gloves since delivery fluids are non-sterile
options.D: Put on sterile gloves first, then wear the gown and face mask afterwards

explanation: Protective barriers must be fully in place before any clinical exposure to blood or amniotic fluid occurs. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which colour receptacle is standard for disposing of infectious clinical waste like blood-soaked cotton balls?

options.A: Black
options.B: Yellow
options.C: Green
options.D: Blue

explanation: Yellow bins or bags are universally designated for infectious and biohazardous clinical waste that requires incineration. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is recapping used injection needles strongly discouraged in midwifery practice?

options.A: It wastes valuable time during busy immunization ward sessions
options.B: It greatly increases the risk of accidental needle-prick injuries
options.C: It ruins the sharp tip of the needle for future procedures
options.D: It makes the syringe impossible to fit inside the safety box

explanation: Trying to guide a used needle back into its cap often results in the midwife accidentally stabbing their own fingers. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h4)

question: What should a midwife do if a sterile instrument accidentally touches a non-sterile surface?

options.A: Wipe it with cotton wool soaked in methylated spirit
options.B: Consider it contaminated and replace it immediately
options.C: Wash it quickly under running tap water and dry it
options.D: Return it to the instrument tray for the next patient

explanation: Once a sterile item touches a non-sterile surface, sterility is broken and it can no longer be used for aseptic procedures. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why are examination couches and delivery tables wiped with disinfectant solutions between different patients?

options.A: To cool down the mattress surface before the next pregnant woman lies down
options.B: To destroy residual pathogens left behind by the previous occupant
options.C: To make the vinyl surfaces look shiny and smell pleasant for visitors
options.D: To prevent the metal parts of the bed from rusting in humid weather

explanation: Routine surface decontamination removes invisible infectious agents that could transfer to the next patient using the bed. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the very first step a midwife should take immediately after sustaining a needlestick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the wound tightly to push out any trapped blood
options.B: Fill out the formal hospital accident report form in the office
options.C: Take a dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics from the treatment room
options.D: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and running water

explanation: Immediate washing removes surface contaminants and reduces the entry of pathogens into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is reporting an occupational exposure to blood so time-sensitive in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Insurance companies refuse claims submitted after twenty-four hours have passed
options.B: Laboratory staff go off duty and cannot test blood samples at night
options.C: Used safety boxes are emptied daily and the specific needle will be lost
options.D: Post-exposure medications work best when started within hours of the contact

explanation: Prophylactic treatment for viruses like HIV must be initiated very quickly after exposure to prevent seroconversion. [learn more](BMP119_U3_T4#BMP119_U3_T4_h6)
